title: The brothers return to battle
intro: Hector ends with a rebuke and a hope for liberation. This short final page completes the sentence begun on page 19.

notes.text: ἀτιμάω 3sg aor opt with ἄν from 521: no fair-minded man would disparage your work in battle. τοι on the previous page supplies your / in your case.
ἄλκιμος, strong / valiant, related to ἀλκή, fighting strength; ἐσσι = εἶ, 2sg pres of εἰμί.
ἑκών nom sg masc, willingly; μεθίημι 2sg pres, relax / slacken your effort. Hector blames willingness, not ability.
κῆρ neut, heart; ἄχνυμαι 3sg pres, is distressed / grieves. κῆρ, not Hector, is the grammatical subject.
σέθεν epic gen = σοῦ; ὑπέρ + gen, about you; αἶσχος neut acc pl, shameful things / reproaches, elided αἴσχεα.
πρός + gen, from the Trojans; εἵνεκα, because of, with gen σεῖο = σοῦ. Their suffering gives the reproaches weight.
εἶμι 1pl pres subj, with short vowel: let us go. Hortatory subj, not an ordinary statement of action.
ἀρέσκομαι / ἀρέσκω 1pl fut mid, make good / settle; τὰ ὄπισθεν, what follows / matters hereafter. We shall settle things later.
αἴ = εἰ, if; δίδωμι 3sg aor subj with κε. ποθι here adds indefiniteness: perhaps / at some point.
ἐπουράνιος, dwelling in heaven; αἰειγενέτης, everlasting. Dat pl agreeing with θεοῖς, for the gods.
κρατήρ acc sg, wine-mixing bowl; ἵστημι aor mid inf, set up for ourselves. ἐλεύθερον: celebrating deliverance, a bowl of freedom.
ἐλαύνω aor ptc acc pl, having driven out; agrees with the understood us, subject of στήσασθαι. Driving out the Achaeans would precede the celebration.
ἐϋκνήμις acc pl, well-greaved; κνημίς, shin guard. The book ends with Hector's hoped-for expulsion of the enemy.
